## Classes

### <a name="noderings"></a>`noderings`

Writes `noderings.yaml` in the Puppet confdir, readable only by its owner. The
noderings_* types read it when a resource has no `api_token` of its own and the
`NODERINGS_TOKEN` environment variable is not set. Declare this class on the
nodes that apply noderings_* resources.

#### Examples

##### Token from Hiera, encrypted with hiera-eyaml

```puppet
class { 'noderings':
  api_token => Sensitive(lookup('noderings::api_token')),
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `noderings` class:

* [`api_token`](#-noderings--api_token)
* [`api_url`](#-noderings--api_url)
* [`organization_id`](#-noderings--organization_id)
* [`config_file`](#-noderings--config_file)
* [`owner`](#-noderings--owner)
* [`group`](#-noderings--group)
* [`ensure`](#-noderings--ensure)

##### <a name="-noderings--api_token"></a>`api_token`

Data type: `Optional[Sensitive[String[1]]]`

The NodeRings service account token. Create one in the NodeRings console under
Organization, Access Control, Service accounts.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-noderings--api_url"></a>`api_url`

Data type: `Stdlib::HTTPSUrl`

The NodeRings API endpoint.

Default value: `'https://api.noderings.com'`

##### <a name="-noderings--organization_id"></a>`organization_id`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

The organization to act in, for tokens that can reach more than one.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-noderings--config_file"></a>`config_file`

Data type: `Stdlib::Absolutepath`

Where to write the settings. The types read `noderings.yaml` in the Puppet confdir.

Default value: `"${settings::confdir}/noderings.yaml"`

##### <a name="-noderings--owner"></a>`owner`

Data type: `String[1]`

Owner of the settings file.

Default value: `'root'`

##### <a name="-noderings--group"></a>`group`

Data type: `String[1]`

Group of the settings file.

Default value: `'0'`

##### <a name="-noderings--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `Enum['present', 'absent']`

`absent` removes the settings file.

Default value: `'present'`

## Resource types

### <a name="noderings_dns_record"></a>`noderings_dns_record`

Manages the records of one name and type in a NodeRings DNS zone, as one set:
the values given replace whatever the set held.

#### Examples

##### Two A records

```puppet
noderings_dns_record { 'www A':
  ensure      => present,
  zone        => 'example.com',
  record_name => 'www',
  type        => 'A',
  values      => ['192.0.2.10', '192.0.2.11'],
  ttl         => 300,
}
```

##### A TXT record at the apex

```puppet
noderings_dns_record { 'spf':
  zone        => 'example.com',
  record_name => '@',
  type        => 'TXT',
  values      => ['v=spf1 include:_spf.example.net -all'],
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `noderings_dns_record` type.

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

Whether the record set should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `ttl`

Time to live in seconds, from 30 to 86400.

Default value: `3600`

##### `values`

Record values. Write hostnames with a trailing dot. TXT values are plain text:
the provider quotes them and splits long ones, so do not add quotes.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `noderings_dns_record` type.

* [`name`](#-noderings_dns_record--name)
* [`provider`](#-noderings_dns_record--provider)
* [`record_name`](#-noderings_dns_record--record_name)
* [`type`](#-noderings_dns_record--type)
* [`zone`](#-noderings_dns_record--zone)

##### <a name="-noderings_dns_record--name"></a>`name`

namevar

A title for the record set. A title of the form `zone/record_name/TYPE`, such as
`example.com/www/A`, also sets `zone`, `record_name` and `type`; `puppet resource`
lists record sets that way.

##### <a name="-noderings_dns_record--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `noderings_dns_record` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet
will usually discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

##### <a name="-noderings_dns_record--record_name"></a>`record_name`

Name relative to the zone, such as www, or @ for the apex. A full name inside the zone also works. Defaults to the
title.

##### <a name="-noderings_dns_record--type"></a>`type`

Record type, such as A, AAAA, CNAME, MX or TXT. Required unless the title is zone/record_name/TYPE.

##### <a name="-noderings_dns_record--zone"></a>`zone`

Name or ID of the zone, which must already exist. Required unless the title is zone/record_name/TYPE.

### <a name="noderings_dns_zone"></a>`noderings_dns_zone`

Manages a DNS zone hosted on NodeRings, and optionally its DNSSEC signing.
`puppet resource noderings_dns_zone` shows the nameservers to set at your registrar.

#### Examples

##### A signed zone

```puppet
noderings_dns_zone { 'example.com':
  ensure => present,
  dnssec => true,
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `noderings_dns_zone` type.

##### `dnssec`

Valid values: `true`, `false`

true signs the zone with DNSSEC, false removes signing. Left unset, signing is not managed.

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

Whether the zone should exist.

Default value: `present`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `noderings_dns_zone` type.

* [`force_delete`](#-noderings_dns_zone--force_delete)
* [`name`](#-noderings_dns_zone--name)
* [`provider`](#-noderings_dns_zone--provider)

##### <a name="-noderings_dns_zone--force_delete"></a>`force_delete`

Valid values: `true`, `false`

With ensure absent, also delete a zone that still has records.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-noderings_dns_zone--name"></a>`name`

namevar

The domain, such as example.com. Case and a trailing dot are ignored.

##### <a name="-noderings_dns_zone--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `noderings_dns_zone` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet will
usually discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

### <a name="noderings_firewall_ruleset"></a>`noderings_firewall_ruleset`

Manages a NodeRings firewall ruleset and its ordered rules. The ruleset holds
exactly the rules given, in order; rules that are not listed are removed.

Each rule is a hash with `direction` (ingress or egress), `action` (accept or
drop), `protocol` (tcp by default), `source` and `destination` (each with
`cidrs`, `address_groups`, `address_group_ids` or `vm_tags`), and optional
`source_ports` and `destination_ports` (one port or one range).

#### Examples

##### Allow SSH from an office and HTTPS from anywhere

```puppet
noderings_firewall_ruleset { 'web':
  ensure => present,
  rules  => [
    { 'direction' => 'ingress', 'action' => 'accept', 'protocol' => 'tcp',
      'destination_ports' => '22', 'source' => { 'cidrs' => ['198.51.100.0/24'] } },
    { 'direction' => 'ingress', 'action' => 'accept', 'protocol' => 'tcp',
      'destination_ports' => '443', 'source' => { 'cidrs' => ['0.0.0.0/0'] } },
  ],
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `noderings_firewall_ruleset` type.

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

Whether the ruleset should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `rules`

Ordered rules, at most 50. See the type description for the keys.

Default value: `[]`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `noderings_firewall_ruleset` type.

* [`force_delete`](#-noderings_firewall_ruleset--force_delete)
* [`name`](#-noderings_firewall_ruleset--name)
* [`provider`](#-noderings_firewall_ruleset--provider)

##### <a name="-noderings_firewall_ruleset--force_delete"></a>`force_delete`

Valid values: `true`, `false`

With ensure absent, also delete a ruleset still attached to virtual machines.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-noderings_firewall_ruleset--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Name of the ruleset.

##### <a name="-noderings_firewall_ruleset--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `noderings_firewall_ruleset` resource. You will seldom need to specify this ---
Puppet will usually discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

### <a name="noderings_ssh_key"></a>`noderings_ssh_key`

Manages an SSH public key stored in a NodeRings organization. `noderings_vm`
installs stored keys on new virtual machines.

#### Examples

##### Store a key

```puppet
noderings_ssh_key { 'deploy':
  ensure     => present,
  public_key => 'ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3Nza... deploy@example',
}
```

##### List the stored keys

```puppet
$ puppet resource noderings_ssh_key
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `noderings_ssh_key` type.

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

Whether the key should be stored.

Default value: `present`

##### `public_key`

The OpenSSH public key, such as the contents of `id_ed25519.pub`. Only the key
type and body are compared; the comment is ignored. A changed key is replaced.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `noderings_ssh_key` type.

* [`name`](#-noderings_ssh_key--name)
* [`provider`](#-noderings_ssh_key--provider)

##### <a name="-noderings_ssh_key--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Name of the key in NodeRings.

##### <a name="-noderings_ssh_key--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `noderings_ssh_key` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet will
usually discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

### <a name="noderings_vm"></a>`noderings_vm`

Manages a NodeRings virtual machine. When no VM has the hostname, Puppet orders
the cheapest marketplace offer that matches `plan`, `country` and `city` (or the
exact `plan_id` and `region_id`). For an existing VM it keeps `tags`,
`firewall_ruleset` and `power_state` as declared. Ordering is billed to the
organization.

#### Examples

##### A web server behind a firewall

```puppet
noderings_vm { 'web-1':
  ensure           => present,
  plan             => 'SC-GC-1C-1G-20',
  country          => 'United States',
  city             => 'Ashburn',
  distro           => 'ubuntu_24_04',
  ssh_keys         => ['deploy'],
  tags             => ['web', 'production'],
  firewall_ruleset => 'web',
}
```

##### List the organization's VMs with their addresses

```puppet
$ puppet resource noderings_vm
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `noderings_vm` type.

##### `distro`

Operating system, such as ubuntu_24_04, debian-13 or rocky_9. Defaults to
ubuntu_24_04 for new VMs. A different distro on an existing VM fails unless
allow_reinstall is true, because reinstalling erases the disk.

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

present orders the VM if it does not exist; absent deletes it.

Default value: `present`

##### `firewall_ruleset`

Name or ID of the firewall ruleset to attach. An empty string detaches it. Left unset, the firewall is not managed.

##### `power_state`

Valid values: `running`, `stopped`

Keep the VM running or stopped. Left unset, power is not managed.

##### `tags`

Tags of the VM. Left unset, tags are not managed.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `noderings_vm` type.

* [`allow_reinstall`](#-noderings_vm--allow_reinstall)
* [`billing_type`](#-noderings_vm--billing_type)
* [`city`](#-noderings_vm--city)
* [`country`](#-noderings_vm--country)
* [`hosting_provider`](#-noderings_vm--hosting_provider)
* [`name`](#-noderings_vm--name)
* [`password`](#-noderings_vm--password)
* [`plan`](#-noderings_vm--plan)
* [`plan_id`](#-noderings_vm--plan_id)
* [`provider`](#-noderings_vm--provider)
* [`provider_id`](#-noderings_vm--provider_id)
* [`region_id`](#-noderings_vm--region_id)
* [`sort`](#-noderings_vm--sort)
* [`ssh_keys`](#-noderings_vm--ssh_keys)
* [`wait_timeout`](#-noderings_vm--wait_timeout)

##### <a name="-noderings_vm--allow_reinstall"></a>`allow_reinstall`

Valid values: `true`, `false`

Reinstall an existing VM whose distro differs. Reinstalling erases the disk.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-noderings_vm--billing_type"></a>`billing_type`

Valid values: `usage`, `subscription`, `free`

How the plan is billed: usage (hourly), subscription (monthly) or free.

Default value: `usage`

##### <a name="-noderings_vm--city"></a>`city`

City of the offer, such as Ashburn.

##### <a name="-noderings_vm--country"></a>`country`

Country of the offer, such as United States.

##### <a name="-noderings_vm--hosting_provider"></a>`hosting_provider`

Only consider offers from this marketplace provider, given by its ID, its
storefront slug (such as acme-hosting) or its name (Acme Hosting, any case).
Left unset, the cheapest matching offer from any provider is ordered. A name
that more than one provider uses fails; give the ID or slug then. (Puppet
reserves the name provider for the resource provider.)

##### <a name="-noderings_vm--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Hostname of the VM. It identifies the VM, so keep it unique in the organization.

##### <a name="-noderings_vm--password"></a>`password`

Root password for a new VM. Pass it as Sensitive.

##### <a name="-noderings_vm--plan"></a>`plan`

Plan code to order, such as SC-GC-1C-1G-20.

##### <a name="-noderings_vm--plan_id"></a>`plan_id`

Exact plan ID to order, instead of plan, country and city.

##### <a name="-noderings_vm--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `noderings_vm` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet will
usually discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

##### <a name="-noderings_vm--provider_id"></a>`provider_id`

Only consider offers from the marketplace provider with this ID. Takes precedence over hosting_provider.

##### <a name="-noderings_vm--region_id"></a>`region_id`

Exact region ID to order, with plan_id.

##### <a name="-noderings_vm--sort"></a>`sort`

Valid values: `price`, `rating`

Order the cheapest matching offer (price) or the best rated (rating).

Default value: `price`

##### <a name="-noderings_vm--ssh_keys"></a>`ssh_keys`

Names or IDs of stored SSH keys (noderings_ssh_key) to install. A new VM needs SSH keys or a password.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-noderings_vm--wait_timeout"></a>`wait_timeout`

Seconds to wait for each operation to finish.

Default value: `900`
